title: Two-Layer AR Coating Optimization: Order and Thickness Sweep
scientific_hypothesis: Within the 40-160 nm thickness constraint, one specific stacking order (Air|TiO2|SiO2|Glass or Air|SiO2|TiO2|Glass) combined with optimized thicknesses will yield a significantly lower arithmetic mean reflectance across 450-700 nm than the alternative order.
design_principle: Antireflection in a two-layer system relies on destructive interference between reflections at the air-coating, coating-coating, and coating-substrate interfaces. The phase shifts upon reflection depend on the relative refractive indices (n_air < n_SiO2 < n_TiO2 < n_glass vs n_air < n_TiO2 > n_SiO2 < n_glass), creating distinct interference conditions for each order that cannot be compensated solely by thickness changes.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be strictly between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for multi-layer stacks
Fresnel equations for normal incidence s-polarization
Transfer Matrix Method for stratified media
expected_advantages: Simultaneously resolves the discrete topology question (order) and continuous geometry question (thickness) within the single allowed route
Directly addresses the user's constraint of using exactly one layer of each material
known_risks: The global minimum may lie outside the 40-160 nm thickness range, leading to a boundary solution that fails the soft target of 0.03
Constant index assumption may deviate from real material dispersion, though required by the prompt
execution_request_english: Optimize a planar two-layer stack on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must contain exactly one layer of SiO2 (Gao) and one layer of TiO2 (Siefke). Evaluate both possible orders: (1) Air | TiO2 (Siefke) | SiO2 (Gao) | Glass and (2) Air | SiO2 (Gao) | TiO2 (Siefke) | Glass. For each order, optimize the individual layer thicknesses within the range [40, 160] nm to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance at normal incidence (0 degrees) with s-polarization over the wavelength range 450-700 nm (5 nm steps). Use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method. Run for up to 2 research rounds with max 64 solver evaluations per round, seed 17. Report the best found stack order, thicknesses, and the resulting mean reflectance spectrum.
